items.title: When you don't understand
items.theme: keeping a conversation going: excuse me, I don't understand, again please, slowly please

phrases.note: A soft way to start. Use it to get attention or before you ask for help.

phrases.text: もう一度お願いします
phrases.note: お願いします (onegai shimasu) is the same "please" you met in yoroshiku onegai shimasu.

phrases.text: もう少しゆっくりお願いします

phrases.note: Same word as wakarimasen, but in the past form. It means the meaning has landed.

dialogue.romanization: Shūmatsu wa nani o shimasu ka.
dialogue.meaning: What will you do on the weekend?

dialogue.text: すみません、わかりません。もう一度お願いします。
dialogue.romanization: Sumimasen, wakarimasen. Mō ichido onegai shimasu.
dialogue.meaning: Sorry, I don't understand. Once more, please.

dialogue.romanization: Shūmatsu wa, nani o shimasu ka.
dialogue.meaning: What will you do on the weekend?

dialogue.text: すみません、もう少しゆっくりお願いします。
dialogue.romanization: Sumimasen, mō sukoshi yukkuri onegai shimasu.
dialogue.meaning: Sorry, a little more slowly, please.

dialogue.romanization: Shūmatsu wa... nani o... shimasu ka.
dialogue.meaning: What... will you do... on the weekend?

dialogue.text: あ、わかりました。ありがとうございます。

practice.question: How would you say "I don't understand"?
You didn't catch what someone said. How do you ask them to say it again?
practice.answer: すみません、もう一度お願いします。(Sumimasen, mō ichido onegai shimasu.)

practice.question: Someone is speaking too fast. What do you say?
practice.answer: すみません、もう少しゆっくりお願いします。(Sumimasen, mō sukoshi yukkuri onegai shimasu.)

practice.question: What is the difference between わかりません (wakarimasen) and わかりました (wakarimashita)?
practice.answer: Wakarimasen means "I don't understand". Wakarimashita means "I understand now" or "got it".

items.say_aloud: Say this three times, slowly: すみません、もう一度お願いします。(Sumimasen, mō ichido onegai shimasu.) It is the one line that keeps any conversation going.
